subject: Re: Overnight latency spikes / temporary SLA bridge plan
messages:
From: Andrew McGregor <amcgregor@cloudledger.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: support@cloudledger.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Overnight latency spikes impacting reconciliation (P1)

Hi Monica,

We're seeing recurring latency spikes overnight that are breaking our end-of-day reconciliation job. These started after the model patch last week; between 02:00–04:30 PST we've had 3 P1s where token latency jumps 4-6x and causes downstream timeouts. Our finance team can't close books until the batch completes.

Can Redwood provide a temporary SLA alignment (lowered P1 response window and a named escalation path) while we work through the join-queue regression? We need a bridge plan for the next 72 hours at minimum.

Attached: recon_spike_20261128.log (text) — includes request IDs and timestamps.

Requests:
- Short-term SLA exception covering 11/29–12/01 to guarantee initial response within 15 minutes overnight (P1).
- A single point of contact for on-call escalation overnight (02:00–05:00 PST).
- Confirmation of monitoring thresholds and a temporary reduction in token-latency alert thresholds to avoid noisy paging.

Thanks,
Andrew McGregor
Head of Platform Reliability, CloudLedger
amcgregor@cloudledger.com

-----Original attachment: recon_spike_20261128.log (text)-----

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Andrew McGregor <amcgregor@cloudledger.com>
Cc: avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Overnight latency spikes impacting reconciliation (P1)

Hi Andrew — thanks for the signal and the log bundle. I pulled this into our infra queue and looped in Avery (on-call lead) and Stephanie (SRE manager).

Short answer: we can stand up a temporary SLA carveout and a named overnight bridge for the next 72 hours, with the following scope:
- Temporary P1 first-response SLA: 15 minutes (02:00–05:00 PST) from 2026-11-29 02:00 PST through 2026-12-02 05:00 PST.
- Named escalation contact: on-call engineer 'Avery Johnson' (Avery will be paged via PagerDuty PD-77821).
- Monitoring tweaks: lower the token-latency alert to the thresholds in the attached bridge doc to reduce false positives.

Proposed immediate steps (actionable):
1) 30-minute bridge call today at 10:00 PST to confirm scope and handoffs — I can host.
2) Avery to accept temporary on-call rotation bump and confirm PD escalation rules.
3) Stephanie to fast-track an SLO exception ticket so our compliance team has a record.

I've attached a short PDF with the proposed bridge plan and the minimal rollback criteria: redwood_bridge_plan_20261129.pdf. If that looks good I'll follow up with the formal SLO exception doc for internal approval.

Would you like us to accept the 72-hour window as-is, or do you want a narrower range?

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

--

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Andrew McGregor <amcgregor@cloudledger.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Overnight latency spikes impacting reconciliation (P1)

Thanks for the ping — I've reviewed the logs and correlated the traces to three increased queue-duration events on our shared inference pool. We're confident this is tied to the recent model patch's scheduling path.

I accept the temporary on-call bump: I'll be the named escalation contact for the window. Operational notes:
- I'll be paged via PagerDuty (PD-77821). If paging fails, page +1 to Stephanie.
- I'll run a targeted capacity carve (move CloudLedger traffic to a reserved slice between 02:00–05:00 PST) to reduce cross-tenant interference.
- We'll throttle non-essential batch requests during the window and enable KV-prefix caching for your reconciliation prefix.

I've created an internal SLO exception request and attached it for audit (slo_exception_request_20261130.docx). I will also open a short-lived dedicated pool and monitor QPS/latency for the 72-hour window. If we see repeated failures (>2 P1s in the window) we'll escalate to a rollback of the recent patch.

Action items assigned:
- Avery: implement reserved slice and configure PD escalation (in progress).
- Stephanie: approve SLO exception and notify compliance.
- Monica: confirm CloudLedger approval and finalize bridge call time.

I'll post updates to the HubSpot ticket and the PagerDuty incident: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/CL-2026-0427/tickets/98123 and https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-77821.

Avery Johnson
On-call Engineer (Redwood Inference)
avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: avery.johnson@redwood.inference.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Overnight latency spikes impacting reconciliation (P1) — bridge confirmed

Andrew — confirmed. Thank you for the fast escalation and for providing the log snippets. Per Avery's note, we will:

1) Apply the temporary P1-first-response SLA (15 minutes) from 2026-11-29 02:00 PST through 2026-12-02 05:00 PST.
2) Route your overnight traffic to a temporary reserved slice (02:00–05:00 PST) to stabilize latency.
3) Name Avery Johnson as the primary escalation contact (PagerDuty PD-77821). If Avery cannot be reached, Stephanie will serve as secondary.
4) Monitor the window closely and provide hourly status updates to this thread and to the HubSpot ticket.

If by 2026-12-02 05:00 PST we have not observed more than two P1-level incidents, we will close the bridge and remove the SLA carveout. If we see a continuing regression, we will initiate rollback of the recent model patch and notify you immediately.

Next: I will send a calendar invite for the 30m bridge at 10:00 PST today and attach the formal SLO exception for your records.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
